content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/plugins/media-session/index.ts / plugin: media session id bridges player transport state to the browser's api, lock-screen media controls, hardware media keys, bluetooth remotes, and os "now playing" widgets. not re-exported from the main entry, import it from the subpath. options currently empty , reserved for future options. rules & restrictions - silently no-ops entirely when is absent node, jsdom, some older webviews, every method is guarded at the top, nothing throws. - position reporting is skipped when duration is zero, , or , some browsers throw on an invalid call. - isn't supported in every browser, the resulting is caught rather than propagated. - safari specifically requires the attribute on the host when embedded for mediasession to activate at all, see the note on the embed plugin. how to extend it to target a native shell capacitor, electron instead of the browser api, subclass with the same and override the platform touchpoints: next steps - plugin: message: the in-player toast surface, for feedback the os chrome doesn't cover.

title: Plugin: Message
description: MessagePlugin: an accessible toast/overlay surface with transient (auto-hide) and persistent (manually-cleared) display modes. Subpath-only import.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/plugins/message/index.ts / plugin: message id is a toast/overlay message surface mounted on the player container, for feedback like "quality switched to 1080p" or "reconnecting...". not re-exported from the main entry, import it from the subpath. options | option | type | default | purpose | |---|---|---|---| | | | | default auto-hide delay for transient messages. | | | | player container | where the toast surface mounts. | rules & restrictions - accessibility is built in, not optional: the toast surface carries and , and persistent messages carry the same attributes. nothing to wire up separately. - persistent messages are time-independent: they stay until is called explicitly with the same , there's no timeout fallback. how to extend it and both accept a plain uses the plugin's default or overrides the default for that one message. calling again, or , cancels an in-flight sequence immediately. next steps - plugin: tab leader: single-tab playback enforcement across multiple open tabs.

title: Plugin: Tab Leader
description: TabLeaderPlugin: single-tab playback enforcement via the Web Locks API cross-tab leader election, so opening the same page twice does not play audio in both. Subpath-only import.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/plugins/tab-leader/index.ts / plugin: tab leader id uses the web locks api to elect one browser tab as the "leader" allowed to play, so opening the same page in two tabs doesn't play audio in both. not re-exported from the main entry, import it from the subpath. options | option | type | default | purpose | |---|---|---|---| | | | | what happens when this tab loses leadership. | | | | | re-request the lock automatically when the tab becomes visible again. | | | | fixed key | scope the lock to a specific player/session instead of the whole origin. | events , , . rules & restrictions - built on the web locks api: safari 15.4+, chrome 69+, firefox 96+. where is absent, the plugin emits and becomes a no-op, playback is unaffected, it just doesn't coordinate across tabs. - the default lock key is global to the entire origin: with no override, only one tab across your whole site plays at a time, not one per player instance. supply to scope it e.g. per media item or per logical session if that global default isn't what you want. how to extend it next steps - adapter: storage: the first of the ten swappable adapter ports, purpose, defaults, and how to extend each.

title: Adapter: Storage
description: IStorage: get/set/remove plus JSON helpers, sync or async either way. Default LocalStorageBackend, with MemoryStorageBackend and IndexedDBBackend shipped alongside it.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/storage/istorage.ts, src/adapters/storage/local-storage.ts, src/adapters/storage/memory.ts, src/adapters/storage/indexed-db.ts / adapter: storage is the port every persisted read/write in the kit goes through, equalizer settings, mixer state, and anything a plugin persists via . swap an adapter walks through replacing it end to end; this page is the reference for the port itself. the interface every method may return its value directly or as a , so a synchronous backend and an asynchronous one satisfy the same interface. plugin code always s regardless of which is active. shipped implementations | class | behavior | |---|---| | | default. synchronous, backed by . falls back to an in-memory map silently when storage is blocked private browsing, quota exceeded. | | | nothing persists past the page session. for tests and ssr. | | | fully async, comfortable with much larger values than 's cap. constructor takes . | rules & restrictions - opens its database lazily on first method call, not at construction, so instantiating it in an environment without node, ssr doesn't crash. method calls reject with a in that environment instead. - a remote/api-backed store for cross-device persistence is a legitimate consumer-supplied implementation, the interface doesn't assume local-only storage. how to extend it implement the five methods against any backing store, swap it in at . see swap an adapter for a complete example including a plugin that reads/writes through it. next steps - adapter: platform: wake lock, network, visibility, and fullscreen/pip, bundled for native-shell portability.

title: Adapter: Platform
description: IPlatform: wake lock, network, visibility, capabilities, and video-only fullscreen/PiP, bundled so a native-shell consumer swaps every browser API in one field.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/platform/iplatform.ts, src/adapters/platform/browser.ts / adapter: platform bundles every primitive the kit would otherwise hardcode against a browser api, so a native-shell consumer capacitor, tauri, electron injects native equivalents in one swap instead of patching five call sites. the interface | field | interface | purpose | |---|---|---| | | | keep the display awake during playback. / / . | | | | online/offline + connection type. / / / . | | | | tab visibility. / . | | | | hardware decode capability, feeds abr. . | | | optional | video only. | | | optional | video only. | rules & restrictions - and are video-only fields. the audio player never touches them; the video player throws a descriptive if either is invoked when the field wasn't supplied. - throws when the screen wake lock api is unavailable, check first if you need to gate the feature instead of catching. - and return on browsers without the network information api firefox, safari as of this writing, not a fabricated number. how to extend it partial overrides compose cleanly, spread the default and replace only the controller you need: full native-shell adapters , , live outside the kit and replace the whole object. next steps - adapter: stream source: the protocol-agnostic handle for a playing or pending media source.

title: Adapter: Stream Source
description: IStreamSource / IStreamFactory: the protocol-agnostic handle for a playing media source. Native and HLS ship built in; register a DASH or custom-protocol factory the same way.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/stream/istreamsource.ts / adapter: stream source is one active instance per playback item, native, hls, or dash, so backend code never branches on protocol. is what decides which kind gets created for a given url, and what a consumer registers to add a new protocol. the factory contract is called for every url the player resolves, only return when your factory can actually handle it. lets a factory decline a url it could technically parse but this device can't decode smoothly. is called at most once per resolution. the source contract exposes / / for lifecycle, for the current , and an optional abr surface , , , for adaptive formats, fixed-bitrate sources simply omit those. events , , , , , flow through / . rules & restrictions - receives a field automatically, injected by , so the created source can pipe fetches through . consumers never set it themselves. - functions installed via compose in registration order, each receives the previous one's output, useful for rewriting manifest urls or injecting auth into segment requests without forking the factory. how to extend it next steps - adapter: url resolver: for urls handed to something that isn't at all.

title: Adapter: URL Resolver
description: IUrlResolver: turns a raw URL into a ResolvedUrl for consumers that cannot attach an Authorization header, a <video>.src, a Cast receiver, a Worker, CSS.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/url-resolver/iurlresolver.ts / adapter: url resolver recipe: provide a custom url resolver walks through a full worked example. this page is the reference for the port itself. the interface carries , , a hint , , , , , , , , or any custom string a plugin passes, and , the built-in behavior, so a custom resolver can delegate for categories it doesn't need to touch instead of reimplementing the default from scratch. resolvedurl the return shape: - : the final string. pass it to a , a worker, or a cast receiver. - : the unparsed input. - , , , , , and for the query. - : the lowercase extension with no leading dot. gate on file type with this rather than splitting on , which breaks on query strings. - : when the input was relative and no was available to absolutize against. rules & restrictions - the default implementation is followed by structured parsing, and that is what calls. a custom resolver replacing the field outright still has that behaviour one call away. - this port is for urls handed to something that is not . if you call yourself, use authfetch: it sets the header rather than encoding credentials into the url. how to extend it swap it at , or at runtime via / to revert. see the recipe for a complete category-branching example. next steps - adapter: translator: the i18n engine port, same swap-at-setup shape.

title: Adapter: Translator
description: ITranslator: t()/language()/addTranslations() and more. Default DefaultTranslator ships built-in core.* strings, English eager and other locales lazy; swap for i18next, FormatJS, or ICU MessageFormat.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/translator/itranslator.ts, src/adapters/translator/translator.ts, src/kit-translations.ts, src/core/mixins/lifecycle.ts / adapter: translator i18n covers how translation resolution works day to day. this page is the reference for the port a whole engine swap replaces. the interface default implementation is a key plus interpolation lookup over a merged bundle table. it is seeded with the kit's own strings. english loads eagerly; every other kit locale loads the first time switches to it. : - : the initial tag, by default - : initial bundles - : async loader for a tag not yet fetched - : custom fallback for an unresolved key - : final fallback, by default. pass to rely on the bcp-47 parent chain alone. rules & restrictions - is what the kit calls on plugin dispose, for prefixed keys. a custom engine has to implement it correctly, or plugin translations never get cleaned up. - returns a , because a real engine may await a loader before the new bundle is ready. callers it rather than assuming the switch is synchronous. how to extend it swap the whole engine when you need pluralization, gender, or icu messageformat. pass your own and the kit uses it as-is, handing it none of the translation config. your engine owns its translation state end to end. so wire , and into your adapter before you pass it. those options seed the built-in only: adapters for i18next and formatjs are meant to live as separate packages outside the kit , , consumers pull only the engine they want. next steps - adapter: cue parser: the same registry-and-default shape, applied to subtitle and lyric formats.

title: Adapter: Cue Parser
description: ICueParser: id, canParse, parse, resolved by CueParserRegistry newest-first. VTT, sprite-VTT, and LRC ship built in; add your own via setup() or at runtime.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/cue-parser/icueparser.ts, src/adapters/cue-parser/registry.ts / adapter: cue parser cue parsers and recipe: register a custom cue parser cover this port in depth. this page is the terse reference. the interface shipped implementations , inline // preserved, cue-setting alignment, sprite-sheet crops via fragments, gated to urls that hint at sprites, , plain or word-level enhanced lrc. rules & restrictions - walks parsers most-recently-registered first and returns the first match. registering a custom parser for an extension a built-in already claims wins resolution without disabling the built-in for other urls. - returning from is a commitment, the registry doesn't fall through to the next parser if then throws. how to extend it next steps - adapter: preload strategy: when and what to prefetch before the outgoing item ends.

title: Adapter: Preload Strategy
description: IPreloadStrategy: shouldPreload() and assetsToPreload() decide when and what to prefetch before the outgoing item ends. Stateless, snapshot-driven, swappable per instance.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/preload/default.ts / adapter: preload strategy controls when the player starts fetching assets for the next queue item, and which assets those are. the interface is a stateless snapshot of , and , so a strategy never reaches into private player state. is . mirrors : , , , , , or a custom string. the auth pipeline uses it to attach the right headers per asset. is , headers only and the default, which suits manifests and sidecars. or , a full fetch, which suits small images and short intros. rules & restrictions - is called on every event while a next item is queued. once it returns , the player suppresses further calls until the cursor moves, so an implementation needs no debounce of its own. - is called when the cursor jumps unexpectedly: a shuffle, a manual , an explicit before the end. it has to abort any in-flight prefetch this strategy started, rather than leave it running against an item nobody wants. default implementation fires at 10s lead by default and returns an empty asset list of its own. music and video players layer domain-specific asset lists on top by providing their own . how to extend it next steps - adapter: transition strategy: how the boundary between outgoing and incoming items is handled.

title: Adapter: Transition Strategy
description: ITransitionStrategy: how the boundary between outgoing and incoming items is handled. CrossfadeTransitionStrategy (music default) and GaplessTransitionStrategy (video default) ship built in.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/preload/default.ts / adapter: transition strategy where preload strategy decides when and what to prefetch, decides how the player crosses from the outgoing item to the incoming one. the interface fires once when first returns , runs every animation frame during the transition window apply volume ramps or curves here, keep it fast and non-blocking, fires once the incoming item is fully primary, and fires if the transition is aborted early a manual , a dispose. is the narrow six-method surface , , , , , a backend needs to host dual-playback, deliberately smaller than the full backend contract so the transition engine works across audio and video without importing per-library types. shipped implementations | class | default for | behavior | |---|---|---| | | music | linear or equal-power volume fade over default 3s before end + default 3s after the incoming item starts. avoids the perceptual volume dip a linear fade has at the midpoint. | | | video | hard-cut at the natural end, no overlap. the incoming item is already warm from preloading, so buffering is near-zero. | rules & restrictions - audio crossfade on a video player is technically possible duck outgoing, raise incoming but needs two simultaneously active elements, which browsers handle inconsistently. opt in explicitly with if you want it, it isn't the video default for that reason. - receiving means no -capable backend is registered, implementations should no-op rather than throw. how to extend it next steps - adapter: shuffle strategy: the permutation the queue applies when shuffled.

title: Adapter: Shuffle Strategy
description: IShuffleStrategy: a single order() method returning a permutation of the queue. MediaList owns cursor-follow, so a strategy only writes the ordering.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/shuffle-strategy/ishufflestrategy.ts / adapter: shuffle strategy controls the permutation applies to the queue. the contract is deliberately minimal. the interface is the current queue, read-only. is the zero-based index of the playing item, or when nothing is active. returns a permutation, same items, no drops, no duplicates. rules & restrictions - cursor-follow is not your responsibility. finding the playing item's new position after the permutation and updating the queue pointer is owned by , so it works correctly for any implementation, a strategy author writes only the reordering logic. - is there so a strategy can pin the currently-playing item return it first, or leave it untouched, and shuffle only the rest, but nothing forces that behavior, a strategy that ignores entirely and reorders everything is equally valid. default implementation singleton instance: is an unbiased uniform-random permutation, ignores , the whole queue reshuffles including the playing item's position. how to extend it next steps - adapter: realtime channel: the transport port behind .

title: Adapter: Realtime Channel
description: IRealtimeChannel / RealtimeFactory: protocol-agnostic realtime transport behind Plugin.websocket(). Default nativeWebSocketAdapter; swap for SignalR, Socket.IO, or a custom transport.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/adapters/realtime/irealtimechannel.ts / adapter: realtime channel is a protocol-agnostic realtime connection handle. is the function shape that creates one, swappable globally or per call. the interfaces : websocket sub-protocol strings, / / reconnection knobs forwarded to the factory; only a factory that implements reconnection reads them, and the built-in native adapter does not, and a per-call override, one connection using a different transport without changing the global default. rules & restrictions - should only be called when , the underlying transport throws otherwise, the port doesn't buffer or queue for you. - resolution order for which factory actually runs: a per-call first, then the player's configured , then the built-in as the final fallback. default implementation wraps the browser's native , with the reconnect/back-off behavior described above layered on top. how to extend it global swap, for every realtime connection the player opens: per-call override, inside a plugin, for one connection using a different transport: next steps - reference: full signatures and types for the composition primitives, config, events, and errors this tour and these reference pages have been building on.

title: Reference: Composition Primitives
description: composeMixins, resolvePlayerConstructor, initPlayerCoreState, the playerCoreMethods aggregate, and every individually-exported mixin group. Curated from src/index.ts.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/compose.ts, src/core/constructor.ts, src/core/state.ts, src/core/index.ts, src/core/kit-version.ts / reference: composition primitives the three functions build a player and quickstart use to turn a plain class into something that behaves like or . composemixins stamps one or more mixin objects onto a prototype, through and . getters and setters land as accessors rather than being triggered during the copy. collisions resolve left to right: a later module in the argument list wins on the same key. so list specific modules after general ones. it is idempotent. calling it twice with the same module overwrites identical descriptors. resolveplayerconstructor the resolution behind all three factory forms: , and . - no id: returns the first registered instance. throws on an empty registry. - a number: indexes the registry's insertion order. throws out of range. - a string: checks the registry first. failing that, resolves and requires a . throws or . ssr-safe: the call is guarded. initplayercorestate seeds every internal slot phase , dispatch stack, cue parser registry, play/volume/repeat/shuffle state, volume , playback rate , and the rest to its canonical starting value. call this once in your constructor, before the instance is usable. kitversion compared against a plugin's at time, mismatches throw . playercoremethods and the individually-exported mixin groups is the tuple of every shared mixin. it is the exact aggregate both real players compose. it bundles 26 mixin groups, and 16 of those are importable individually from the public entry. the other 10 are internal building blocks, meant to be taken as part of the aggregate rather than recomposed piecemeal: stream registration, media tracks, device detection, audio output, cast state, abr, metrics, loading, activity, and generic dom helpers. individually exported, for composing a narrower surface than the full aggregate: · · · · · · · · · · · · · · · most consumers want the full aggregate, as every page in build a player does, composing a subset is an advanced move for a genuinely minimal use case. next steps - title: Native quickstart
description: The engine, on Kotlin and Swift, for an app that draws its own player.
content: core ships one thing and only one: the engine, with no chrome on it. an application that wants controls takes the video or music package, whose drop-in view is a player. an application that has already drawn its own takes this and gets the state machine, the event bus, the queue and the plugin runtime with nothing on top. everything the reference lists is on that object. what it announces reaches anything subscribed, which is how a chrome, a notification and a cast session stay in agreement without knowing about each other. the testing kit the stand-ins ship as their own coordinate, so a consumer testing their own integration writes none of their own. it carries , a with a real event bus and a real plugin registry, fakes for storage, sockets and http, and , which registers a plugin, hands it to you, tears it down and asserts the bus came back to where it started. every test written through it is also a leak test at no cost to the author. the debug view records the firehose into a bounded buffer, and the overlay renders it over whatever is playing. it answers what a breakpoint cannot: what happened just before the thing that went wrong. the compose overlay is in and the swiftui one in the product, separate from the engine so a debug view has to be asked for by name rather than arriving with it. next the methods reference lists the shared surface both players carry, and the error codes are the whole trio's.

title: Migrating to the native core
description: Moving Kotlin or Swift code off a hand-rolled player state machine.
content: the code this replaces is rarely called a player. it is a view model holding a boolean and a position, a service holding a queue, and a screen holding the rules about which of the two wins. splitting them was never a decision; they grew where they were needed. what moves the state machine, the queue cursor, the event bus and the plugin runtime. those four are what core is. anything in your code doing one of them has a counterpart here, and keeping both is how the two come to disagree. the engine does not move. is a port with three implementations already written, and a fourth is a class you supply. kotlin replace reads first. a view model that exposed exposes instead, and everything binding to it keeps working. replace writes second: a screen that flipped a boolean and told the engine now calls and lets the announcement do the telling. replace the queue last, because it is the one with rules in it. shuffle, repeat and what plays next are all here, and moving them one at a time leaves a window where both are deciding. swift arrives through the xcframework with every kotlin default argument spelled out, because defaults do not cross to objective-c. the constructor takes twelve arguments and most of them are nil; the surface file in the repository writes them out in full so the cost is visible rather than described. verifying the move the testing kit is the thing that makes this safe to do incrementally. register what you moved as a plugin, drive it with , and the harness tells you whether it cleaned up after itself. a screen that used to hold state and now holds a subscription is exactly the shape that leaks.

title: What is nomercy-video-player
description: A headless, event-driven video engine with adaptive HLS streaming, VTT and ASS/SSA subtitle rendering, fullscreen/PiP/theater display modes, and a plugin system, built on nomercy-player-core.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/index.ts, src/types.ts / what is nomercy-video-player is a video engine. it ships no ui. you get the transport and a typed api. you build the interface, or drop in the official prebuilt one. what it handles for you: - adaptive hls, with the backend chosen per browser - subtitles in two very different formats: plain vtt, and ass/ssa with embedded fonts - fullscreen, picture-in-picture and theater modes - quality selection on top of adaptive bitrate - chapters, scrub-preview thumbnails and segment playback - a plugin system it is built on /nomercy-player-core, which carries lifecycle, queueing, plugins, translations and auth. this library adds the video backend, and the methods that only mean something when watching: display modes, subtitle and audio track selection, quality, chapters and segment windows. who it's for anything where someone watches: a streaming client, a live-event page, a video tile in a dashboard. reach for it when you want the ui to be yours rather than someone else's restyled, or when you want the official overlay without writing one. building a player that is neither video nor music? start with /nomercy-player-core. why it exists watching has a problem listening does not: browsers disagree. hls plays natively only in safari. everywhere else it needs . a subtitle track can be a plain vtt cue, or a full ass/ssa script with embedded fonts, positioning and karaoke timing that no browser renders on its own. this library absorbs both behind one typed surface. picks native hls or per browser, so never branches on user agent. renders vtt, and brings in a real libass renderer the moment a track needs ass/ssa. queueing, transport, volume, auth and plugins are not specific to watching, so they come from the core. the setup, then freedom, model create an instance, call once, wait for it, then build whatever ui you want. is the factory. it returns the existing instance for an id already in use, or mounts a new one into the with that id. is the only strict step. it walks a fixed sequence: config snapshot, plugin registration, stream, auth, playlist, media readiness. it primes a start item as soon as the playlist is not empty. calling it twice throws, so a half-configured player is not a state you can reach. after resolves, nothing is required of you. build controls with the typed methods, or add plugins for a control bar, touch input, cast or media session. every path uses the same , and . what you get - created through the factory, generic over your playlist item type. - adaptive hls streaming: native hls on safari, everywhere else. the import is dynamic, so safari pays nothing, and the call surface is the same either way. - subtitle rendering across two formats renders vtt out of the box, brings in a libass renderer for embedded-font ass/ssa. - display modes , , and , plus aspect ratio control / / / . - quality and abr and for manual selection on top of the backend's own adaptive bitrate engine. - chapters, thumbnails and segments: typed chapter navigation, vtt-sprite scrub previews, and for intro loops or chapter-range playback. - a drm hook coordinates eme license acquisition for widevine, fairplay, and playready, degrading quietly in environments without eme. - plugin system: a prebuilt control bar , touch input , keyboard and remote bindings, cast and media session. all opt-in. - everything from lifecycle, queue, transport, volume, translations, and auth aware fetch. where it sits : backend, fullscreen/pip/theater, subtitles, quality, chapters, segments.' , n: 1, name: 'nomercy-player-core', pkg: 'dependency', knows: 'lifecycle, queue, transport, plugins, i18n, auth.' , /> next steps - quick start install the player and get a real video playing.

title: Quick Start
description: Install nomercy-video-player and play a real HLS video with the baseUrl pattern. One copy-paste example that works first try.
content: video player: quick start this gets a real video loaded and ready in the preview below: sintel, streamed over hls, using the baseurl pattern every nomercy player and app is built around. install that's the only package you need. is a regular dependency pulled in through , so npm installs it for you; the player dynamically imports it for every browser except safari, which plays hls natively. there is no peer dependency to add by hand. play your first video here it is loaded for real: sintel, streamed over hls, ready on the first frame. press play in the preview to start it. below the player is the exact code that produced it, ready to copy: :::snippetfile="quickstart" runnable preview="first" ::: add a to your page for that code to mount into. the player loads the first item as it mounts, so the preview above sits ready on sintel's first frame with nothing set to autoplay. the flag gives it the native play button you press to start. only decides whether that already-loaded item also begins playing. pairs with it, because browsers block autoplay with sound. leave both off, as this example does, and drive playback from your own ui with on a user gesture. mounts into , or returns the instance already registered under that id. calling it twice is always safe. the baseurl pattern is the one config field every playlist should set. item paths above stay relative, exactly the shape a real media server sends, and the player prepends as a plain string prefix, keeping the whole base path: - the server sends the base with no trailing slash and each item path with a leading slash . - move to a different server, a different environment, or a signed-url cdn, and you change one config value; nothing in your catalogue is hardcoded to today's origin. - never pre-join an absolute url into an item yourself. that is the player's job, and doing it twice breaks the moment the base changes. next steps - guided tour: transport: play, pause, and seeking, the first stop on the full method surface. - build a player: put a real overlay ui on top of the player, one control at a time.

title: Transport
description: play(), pause(), stop(), togglePlayback(), next()/previous(), rewind()/forward()/restart(), and seeking through time(seconds).
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/index.ts, packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/transport.ts, src/core/mixins/time.ts / transport doesn't reimplement transport. every method below is 's transport contract: a cancellable dispatch, then a call into the video backend. video adds nothing to the surface here, only a real element for it to drive. play, pause, stop , , , and all return a that resolves once the backend call settles. / move the queue cursor and load, seeks to and resumes. every one of these accepts an bag and take the wider , which extends it. defaults to and gets stamped onto the emitted event, so a connect plugin syncing playback across devices can tell its own remote-triggered apart from a real click. seeking through time reads the current position in seconds. seeks to a new one. there is no separate . position is reported by two different events, for two different reasons. ordinary playback ticks the event per frame, plus the throttled event. a deliberate jump fires the cancellable → → cycle. it is the same split the web platform draws between and /. the tick against the jump: and compute a relative target from the current position and run it through the same → → cycle; both default to a -second step when called with no argument. seeks to a position expressed as – percent of , the calculation a progress bar's click handler would otherwise have to do by hand: guard first every transport method calls the kit's guard before doing anything else. calling before resolves, or after , throws a typed instead of silently reaching into missing state, the same contract core: transport contract documents in full, including the / shape of the event. see it running mounts the browser's own bar. its play, pause and scrubber call the same methods this page describes, and nothing else is wired. :::snippetfile="video-tour-transport" preview="first" ::: next steps - volume: volume, mute/unmute, and the volume gain state a slider or mute icon reads.

title: Volume
description: volume(), mute()/unmute()/toggleMute(), volumeUp()/volumeDown(), and volumeState(), the gain surface a slider or mute icon reads.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/volume.ts / volume volume is another kit surface inherits unchanged, there's no video-specific volume behavior, the backend just needs a real / gain to move. reading and setting the level reads the current level as a number in ; sets it, clamped to that range, and returns a once the backend applies it: set an initial level through , a number on the same 0-100 scale that defaults to . a player with no starts at full gain, so read a saved preference into that config field, or call yourself after if you'd rather set it later. mute and are absolute; flips based on the current state. all three dispatch first, same cancellable shape as transport, and no-op never dispatch when already in the target state: and nudge the level by by default, clamped to the same as a direct call, the pair a keyboard shortcut or remote's volume rocker binds to. reading the gain stage returns a typed or , the value a mute-icon component reads instead of tracking its own boolean, since it stays correct even when something other than that icon a keyboard shortcut, a connect sync changes the mute state: , , and / events carry / payloads respectively, subscribe to those instead of polling the getters from a render loop. see it running the native bar's volume slider and mute button drive and underneath. the player starts muted, which is why the bar opens on the muted glyph. :::snippetfile="video-tour-volume" preview="first" ::: next steps - the queue & playlist: the cursor-aware list , , and read from and move through.

title: The Queue & Playlist

reads the active item, moves the cursor and loads it. reads the cursor's position, its size: / read what / see transport would load, without moving the cursor or triggering a load, useful for a "coming up next" thumbnail. mutating the queue every mutation method below fires a typed event , , ... that a reactive playlist ui subscribes to instead of re-reading after every call. | method | what it does | | --- | --- | | | add to the end. | | | add to the front. | | | add at a specific position. | | / | remove by id or position. | | | reorder in place. | | | empty the queue. | | | randomize order; the cursor follows the currently-playing item to its new position. | | | sort with your own comparator. | removing the item before the cursor decrements the cursor automatically, so it keeps pointing at the same logical item, none of these ever silently jump playback to the wrong entry. playitem and playnow races: fires a fire-and-forget , and a called immediately after can reach the backend before the source is even set. and exist to close that race, both route through internally, which only calls inside the resolved 's own continuation. see it running three real films in one queue, the same catalogue the code below reads. the native bar plays whichever one the cursor is on; the methods above are what move it. :::snippetfile="video-tour-queue" preview="first" ::: next steps - subtitles & text tracks: subtitles, subtitle, and defaultsubtitlelanguage.

title: Subtitles & Text Tracks
description: subtitles(), subtitle(), subtitleStyle(), cycleSubtitles(), defaultSubtitleLanguage, and where the cue text actually gets painted.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/media-tracks.ts, packages/nomercy-video-player/src/plugins/subtitle-overlay/index.ts / subtitles & text tracks subtitle selection and subtitle rendering are two separate concerns. most of this page is selection: listing tracks, picking one, styling the text. that is kit surface, 's , reading and writing state. and are the two video-only additions, called out below. painting cue text on screen is a plugin's job. for vtt, for ass/ssa with embedded fonts. build a player: selectors hand-builds the picker that calls . pair it with to render the text. neither renderer is loaded by default. selecting a track without one changes state correctly and paints nothing. listing and selecting tracks returns the track list for the active item; reads the current selection as or when off. selects by index, turns subtitles off: walks in one call. that is what a keyboard shortcut or a remote's cc button binds to, instead of resolving the next index by hand. returns or , for a ui that only needs to know whether any track is active. both are defined on the video player rather than the kit. auto-selecting a language on auto-selects a track once the manifest resolves, matching an exact bcp-47 tag first, then a prefix matches a track tagged : no match leaves subtitles off, silently, no error and no fallback track forced on. styling reads the current ; merges a partial patch onto it and emits with the merged result, the event listens for to repaint every active cue immediately: the kit only owns the in-memory value and the event, persisting a user's choice across sessions is your app's job or a preference plugin's. see it running sintel carries four real subtitle tracks on its own field. picks english once the manifest resolves, and paints the cues over the video. :::snippetfile="video-tour-subtitles" preview="first" ::: next steps - audio tracks: audiotracks, audiotrack, and the same selection shape applied to embedded audio renditions.

title: Audio Tracks

content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/media-tracks.ts, packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/player-state.ts, packages/nomercy-video-player/src/index.ts / audio tracks an hls manifest can carry more than one audio rendition per item, alternate languages, a commentary track, a stereo/5.1 pair. and mirror the subtitle surface from subtitles & text tracks exactly: same index-based selection, same shape, same auto-select config field. listing and selecting unlike subtitles, audio tracks have no "off" state, one is always active once the manifest resolves. walks the list and wraps around at the end instead of stopping, since there's no off position to land on. default language on auto-selects a track once the manifest parses, same bcp-47 exact-then-prefix matching uses: reading the selection mode returns when no explicit choice has been made yet the backend's own default rendition is active or once a consumer or preference plugin has picked one, the state a "reset to default" menu item reads before deciding whether to show itself. see it running sintel's manifest carries a single embedded audio rendition, so there is nothing to switch between here. the player below is the plain config; the calls above are the same ones a multi-language item answers. :::snippetfile="video-tour-audio-tracks" preview="first" ::: next steps - quality levels: qualitylevels, quality, and the 'levels' event a bitrate selector waits for.

title: Quality Levels
description: qualityLevels(), quality(), defaultQuality, the levels/level-switched events, and bandwidth()/canPlay() for building your own bitrate selector.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/media-tracks.ts, src/core/mixins/abr.ts / quality levels adaptive bitrate is on by default, or safari's native hls keeps switching renditions to match bandwidth without you doing anything. this page is for when you want a manual quality menu on top of that. listing levels returns the manifest's bitrate renditions once the event has fired, each with , and / when the manifest provides them. also returns renditions the current device can't decode, useful for showing them disabled in a menu rather than hiding them entirely: reading and setting the selection returns for a manually-picked level, or the string while abr is driving. locks a specific level; hands control back to the backend: setting a level emits immediately video-specific, fired before the backend confirms the switch and once the backend actually applies it, subscribe to the latter for a "now playing at 1080p" toast, the former if you need to reflect the request instantly in a ui without waiting on the network. default quality on applies once after the first manifest parse, either the kit's own default, so setting it explicitly is only useful for readability or a fixed level index: bandwidth and capability checks reads the backend's current estimate in bits per second. that is the number abr decides against. replaces the estimator with your own, for a measurement shared across several players on one page. asks the platform's whether a content profile is decodable, by , resolution, bitrate and framerate. ask before offering it in a menu. see it running running against sintel's real bitrate ladder. the native bar has no level picker, so the calls above are how you would put one in front of it. :::snippetfile="video-tour-quality" preview="first" ::: next steps - chapters: chapters, seektochapter, and playsegment for arbitrary time windows.

title: Chapters
description: chapters(), seekToChapter(), nextChapter()/previousChapter(), and playSegment()/clearSegment() for looping or holding an arbitrary time window.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/index.ts playsegment, clearsegment, packages/nomercy-player-core/src/core/mixins/media-tracks.ts / chapters chapters come from the item's typed field: canonical , seconds set directly, or the server's wire format's millisecond-based array, which converts to the canonical shape at queue-ingest time. is a plain synchronous getter over whatever list is already on the active item, there's no async fetch to wait on. listing and navigating returns the resolved list, each entry an , , and in seconds, plus a display title. jumps directly; / step relative to the current position, not the last chapter you explicitly selected, so they stay correct even after a manual scrub: reads the chapter containing the current position. it returns when none covers it: before the list resolves, or in a gap the safety net has not backfilled. only emits with . and inherit that, because they route through it. playback crossing a boundary on its own does not fire the event. to follow the active chapter during ordinary playback, read on each tick. the event fires once the list resolves. returns for an item with no field, a chapter-marker ui can render unconditionally and simply show nothing when the list is empty. malformed lists get a safety net. once the duration is known, any span the list fails to cover is backfilled: a lead-in before the first chapter, a hole between two, or a tail after the last. each filler carries a translated fallback title, "chapter" in english, and . so markers and always work against a list spanning the whole timeline. a list that already covers the duration passes through untouched, and an empty list stays empty. the net only catches lists claiming partial coverage. arbitrary time windows chapters are one instance of a more general primitive: seeks to and watches every event for . when the boundary is reached, always fires first, then decides what happens: | | behavior | | --- | --- | | | seek back to and keep playing. | | | pause at , last frame stays visible. | | | emit the boundary event and let playback continue naturally. | this isn't chapter-specific, it's the same primitive an intro-skip loop, a disc-menu state window, or a highlight-reel scrubber would use. any previously active segment window is replaced immediately when you call again; stops watching without moving playback. see it running sintel ships real chapter marks on its own field. the player below is the plain config they arrive with; the methods above are what navigates them. :::snippetfile="video-tour-chapters" preview="first" ::: next steps - playback state & events: playstate, bufferstate, and the full event surface a ui subscribes to.

the quickstart loads the first, sintel: :::snippetfile="video-recipe-react-app" live="false" ::: config identity is deliberately left out of the effect's dependency array. objects are rarely stable across renders. an inline literal is a new object every time. re-running on every render is both wrong and wasteful: it throws once the player is already set up. above memoizes it with , keyed on , rather than fighting the hook. strictmode guards with . react 18 strictmode double-invokes effects in development: mount, cleanup, mount, synchronously. that happens before the cleanup's fire-and-forget has resolved, because a synchronous cleanup cannot it. without the guard, the second mount's resolves the same still-registered instance, and calling on it again throws . the guard fixes that crash. it does not close every strictmode edge case: a brief listener gap is still possible between the first mount's deferred clearing listeners and the second mount's subscriptions. that window is double-invoke behaviour, and it is stripped from production builds. context provider for a shared instance for a layout where a persistent mini-player and a full-screen view share one instance, wrap the hook in a context rather than calling it twice. creation happens in the render body, the sanctioned lazy--init pattern. disposal happens in the effect's cleanup. checking on every render recovers from a strictmode double-invoke disposing the shared instance out from under a still-mounted provider: :::snippetfile="video-recipe-react-provider" live="false" ::: next steps - recipe: svelte integration: the same events-into-state pattern as a svelte store.

title: Recipe: Persistence & Resume
description: Save watch position from the progress event, resume from item.progress and autoPlay across sessions, and the WatchProgress shape that drives it.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/types.ts, src/player/start-selection.ts, src/player/normalize-item.ts / recipe: persistence & resume the player never persists watch position. it reads if your data carries it, and it emits so you can save new values. the storage round-trip is your app's job. this recipe covers both halves: writing progress out as it plays, and feeding it back in so the next session resumes where the last one stopped. saving progress as it plays fires , throttled by 5 seconds by default, cheap enough to persist on every fire without debouncing again in your own code: fires far more often every native , dozens of times a second and is the wrong signal for a persistence write, it exists for scrubber ui, not for storage. always save from . the watchprogress shape attach the saved record to the matching field on the item the next time you build a playlist, this is the exact shape expects: what setup does with it, and what autoplay gates every with a non-empty playlist picks a start item from on its own. no extra config, and it happens whether or not is set. the rules: - the most recently watched item wins, by . - an item over 90% watched rolls forward to the next one, rather than replaying the credits. - anything else resumes at . rides the load down to the backend, so the stream starts fetching at the offset. there is no play-then-seek flash. is the one thing this does not decide for you. it only says whether the primed item also starts playing, or the player mounts paused on the right item and position. this means the feed-in half of the recipe is just: know the last-watched item and its before you call . everything else, picking which item, deciding whether to resume or roll forward, is already built. handling items outside the initial playlist 's selection only runs once, over the items present at . if your app resumes a title that is not in the queue yet a deep link, a "continue watching" row loaded separately, skip the config field and drive it directly: see it running this demo proves the persistence half, not the built-in path above. it sets and hand-rolls its own resume: read on mount, then call once confirms the source can be seeked. a docs preview cannot reload the page for you the way a real app's next visit would. the badge shows the value read on mount, then updates on every tick. reload this page, or open it in a new tab, and the badge still reflects the position your last visit saved. it re-reads the same key. :::snippetfile="video-recipe-resume-playback" live="false" ::: next steps - the mixin method: 1. arm. / set the scrub flag on the activity state, so the chrome cannot hide mid-drag. 2. paint. / paint the pop timestamp, sprite thumbnail, covering chapter title and move the hover fill. while armed they also drag the nipple, without seeking yet. 3. seek once, at release. a on , a , or a click computes the time from the pointer position and calls . the lives on , not the bar, so a drag that ends outside still finalizes. while scrubbing, the event handler skips its progress updates so the clock cannot yank the nipple back. the buffered fill is , repainted on every event, wrapped in a try/catch because a detaching sourcebuffer can throw mid-read. chapters change the rendering mode. with chapters present, the bar gains , the single buffer fill hides, and each chapter gets its own marker div holding four layers: background, buffer, hover, and progress. a marker spans , and that 2 pixel gap is what draws the dividers. fills are painted with . a value before the chapter's range is , past it , inside it the fraction of the span. progress, buffered, and hover all reuse the same fill function on different layers. clicking a marker calls . markers rebuild on the event, on , and on item change, whichever arrives last wins. sprite seek thumbnails plus the sprite mixin own the preview thumbnail in the scrub pop. the sprite url resolves from the playlist item: the typed field first, then a legacy sidecar entry. the manifest is a vtt whose cue bodies read . parsing delegates to core's . both requests route through the plugin's authenticated : the vtt as text, the sprite image as an turned into a object url. the detour exists because a bare cannot carry an header. the image is preloaded so the first hover paints instantly. loads are race-guarded with an incrementing token: a playlist jump mid-load discards the stale result and revokes its object url rather than painting the previous film's thumbnails. painting is on a fixed-size div. the object url is revoked on the next item and on dispose. responsive breakpoints runs a four-rule visibility pass over the bottom row on every resize, orientation change, and hover-capability change: 1. consumer opt-out: a button disabled in never shows. 2. content gating: a button marked no subtitle tracks, one audio track, no chapters is skipped without counting its width. 3. orientation: in portrait, the set is forced off. 4. container fit: walk most-important first, accumulate estimated widths 40 px per button, plus 96 px for the volume slider's hover expansion on hover-capable devices, with 148 px reserved for the time labels and padding, and hide everything that no longer fits. a on the container drives the pass. and feed rules 3 and 4. both stamp and attributes on the container for css to key off. the active breakpoint name is stamped as , and crossing a boundary emits . the volume slider has its own mode logic here too: - is pure css expand-on-hover. - is a click-toggled popup above the mute button, with its own mute row. - the default picks vertical whenever the device has no hover or the player is 520 px or narrower, re-evaluated on resize. icon and button state is a set of pure functions, each receiving only the dom refs and scalars it needs, no plugin instance. the mixin binds them to the plugin's refs and player. one convention runs through all of them: a non-default state gets the class, which the stylesheet uses to force the filled icon variant. it lights up for: - playback rate away from 1 - a manually pinned quality - an active subtitle track - a non-default audio track - pip engaged - an aspect ratio other than aria-labels carry the dynamic part. the speed button appends the rate when non-default, the quality button appends the playing level's label. the volume icon derives from mute state and level together: muted or zero shows the muted glyph, below 30 low, up to 60 medium, above that high. quality has one extra wrinkle: the icon and menu distinguish the requested level from the playing one. the requested value is what the user picked, often . the playing index is cached from the event, with a fallback peek at before the first switch lands. levels are matched by their field, never array position, because filters unsupported codecs. transport state the mixin owns time, duration, capability gating, and enable/disable logic. capability gating hides buttons whose feature the current item cannot use, via , so the responsive pass skips their width: - subtitles with zero tracks, unless rows exist, which keep the button reachable on their own - audio with one track or fewer - quality with fewer than two levels - chapter buttons with no chapters - playlist with fewer than two queue items the settings button itself hides when everything it would contain is empty. the matching main-menu category rows hide with their buttons. all of it re-runs on , , , , , and item change. enablement is finer than visibility: - / disable at the queue edges - rewind disables at time zero - forward disables within a quarter second of the end - the chapter buttons disable when no chapter exists in their direction one-second tolerance disabled buttons get both and . display-state visibility composes on top: theater hides in fullscreen or pip it is meaningless there, and the top-bar buttons hide in pip. a config opt-out always wins over state-driven showing. the remaining-time label toggles between countdown and total duration on click, and the choice persists through the plugin's scoped storage under the key . feedback overlays the mixin owns the spinner and the message line. the message element lives on the player container, not the overlay, deliberately: a "loading…" line must survive the chrome auto-hiding. playback feedback is event-driven. and show a buffering state, a new shows loading, and , , or clear it. an event shows the error line. the initial "loading…" only shows when the player actually has something queued, because a player can legitimately mount idle. the busy class goes on the plugin's own center wrapper, never the container, whose playback-state classes belong to core. the same message line doubles as the consumer toast surface. any code can show one through plain player events, no plugin reference needed: a toast with set dismisses itself; playback feedback instead clears when playback recovers. keyboard shortcuts overlay the key toggles a dialog listing the key bindings; closes it, and with a menu open closes the menu first. other plugins toggle it by emitting the plugin's own event. a one-time hint toast "press ? for shortcuts" shows on the first per browser session, tracked in . live option changes the plugin listens to its own event. re-emitting it with new options re-applies , re-runs capability gating so a live change takes effect, and re-renders the rows. those rows are the one main-menu row kind built for repaint. a consumer can add "cast to device…" after its cast sdk finishes an async probe and see the row appear without a rebuild. rules & restrictions - loading alongside native or 's own key bindings without disabling one results in doubled ui or conflicting handlers, pick one control surface per platform. - menu-driven and cycle-driven is a deliberate split. quality, subtitles, audio, speed and aspect ratio open a menu on click, because each has a list. theater, pip and fullscreen are binary toggles. and friends are for remote-control and key-bind contexts where there is no list to pick from, not the pointer default. how to extend it styling goes through plain css against the plugin's own class names. loads once per page regardless of player count, so override selectors in your own stylesheet rather than forking the plugin. for behavior beyond what options cover, subclass and override the lifecycle hooks or add your own plugin that reads : next steps - plugin development: the video-specific surfaces every group above builds on. - plugin handbook: the shared toolkit, , , , , , and the rest. - plugin: touch zones: the touch-input counterpart, coordinated with this plugin's auto-hide cycle through the shared event.

content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/plugins/tv-key-handler/index.ts / plugin: tv key handler id adapts /nomercy-video-player/plugins-adapters/key-handler for tv remote input. it inherits the full desktop default set color buttons, universal media keys, modifier seeks, chapters, speed, frame-advance, subtitle size, stop and overrides only the groups that behave differently when the input device is a remote, not a keyboard with focusable page elements. options | option | type | default | purpose | |---|---|---|---| | | | | seconds / seek on tv. color-button seeks 30/60/90/120s are fixed and unaffected. | | | | | how long the info osd stays visible before auto-dismissing. | every option from the base /nomercy-video-player/plugins-adapters/key-handler , , , , , still applies. what changes from the desktop set | group | desktop behavior | tv behavior | |---|---|---| | / | gated off when assumed to control page focus instead. | seek directly, each. the host page is expected to remove focus from interactive elements before mounting this plugin. | | / | gated off on tv in the desktop plugin. | enabled, / fire directly so a web-based tv shell can forward them to the system mixer or handle them in-player. | | / | cycles aspect ratio silently. | cycles aspect ratio and shows an osd confirmation, there is no visible control bar on a tv to reflect the change otherwise. | | help | bound as , calls directly via . | bound as plain not and emits instead, a tv shortcuts overlay registers independently from the desktop ui one. | new groups this plugin adds on top of the inherited set: - : shows an osd with title, current chapter, time and remaining time. also emits with the same data so a tv shell can render its own overlay instead of or alongside the built-in osd message. - : emits with the current playback time. the plugin does not persist bookmarks itself, that is the consumer's job; a missing listener is a silent no-op. rules & restrictions - osd messages route through when it is mounted on the player, and always also emit for consumers that prefer the event surface over adding . - all bindings call local player methods directly. a nomercy connect integration that wants remote commands routed through a socket instead calls inherited from the kit base to swap individual bindings, this plugin has no built-in awareness of connect. - translations the info osd strings, aspect-ratio label, chapter labels are auto-discovered from the plugin's own bundle. the static field overrides the base 's rather than extending it, so registering this plugin merges only its own keys into the player's shared translation table namespaced under , removed again on dispose. how to extend it override one group the same way as the desktop plugin, or add a tv-only group entirely: next steps - plugin: desktop ui: the overlay the desktop key handler's opens via .

title: Plugin: Cast Sender

content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/plugins/cast-sender/index.ts / plugin: cast sender id is a thin, two-method specialization of the kit's /nomercy-player-core/plugins-adapters/cast-sender, which owns everything medium-agnostic: sdk probing, session lifecycle, event mirroring, resume-on-disconnect. this subclass only supplies the two things that differ between video and music: the default mime type, and how a becomes cast metadata. options same the kit plugin defines, , , , , , , see plugin: cast sender core for the full table. defaults to here on the music player's own subclass unless you override it explicitly. events same as the base: , , , , , . what the video subclass builds reads only fields already on the canonical : | item has... | metadata built | |---|---| | set non-empty string | falls back to if the sdk build lacks the tv-show constructor, from , / set when present. | | unset or empty | plain , only, is not set on this path. | | | resolved through auth-aware, respects and set as the metadata's . | rules & restrictions - all the base plugin's restrictions apply unchanged: chrome/chromium web sender sdk only, requires / already loaded on the page, volume converted from the player's 0-100 scale to the sdk's native 0-1 float divided by 100 at the boundary, clamped to spec range. - consumers carrying application-specific fields beyond the canonical a server-specific , for instance should subclass this plugin and override themselves rather than expecting it to read fields it was never typed against. - and this plugin are separate, unlinked mechanisms. is the kit's own coarse handoff, it drives the cast sdk directly and knows nothing about . adding this plugin does not wire it into , and calling does not go through this plugin's / metadata pipeline. pick one cast strategy per app. how to extend it next steps - plugin: media session: the os lock-screen equivalent, built on the same title/show/season metadata fields.

title: Plugin: Subtitle Overlay
description: SubtitleOverlayPlugin: renders the subtitleCue event stream as a positioned, WebVTT-layout-accurate DOM overlay, pooled per active cue, styled from subtitleStyle().
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/plugins/subtitle-overlay/index.ts / plugin: subtitle overlay id is the vtt rendering half of subtitle support. it turns the player's stream into a styled, positioned dom tree above the video. those cues arrive either as sidecar vtt parsed by the kit, or as native cuechange forwarded by the backend. it is a pure consumer. where cues come from is decided upstream, in the kit and the video backend. this plugin paints what it is handed. options currently has no configurable fields, add the plugin as-is: visual customization goes through see subtitles & text tracks, not plugin options, the plugin repaints every active cue immediately on the event. dom tree and cue pooling and pairs are pooled, one per active cue. two cues active at different positions render as two independently positioned boxes, the way a browser's native vtt renderer handles simultaneous cues. where cues would collide, the later one is nudged along the line axis. that mirrors the webvtt collision-avoidance step, rather than letting two lines paint over each other. the overlay itself is sized and positioned to the actual video display rectangle , letterbox-fit under , not the container, so subtitles never sit inside letterbox padding on a wide container playing a narrower-aspect video. cue geometry cue , , and map to css following the webvtt 1.0 layout algorithm. horizontally, and derive from , and an alignment anchor of 0, 0.5 or 1 for start, center and end. vertically, the anchor picks or from which half of the safezone falls in. that approximates the native renderer's overflow fallback. the safezone insets 5% top and bottom, 3% left and right. it is calibrated for widescreen delivery rather than the crt-era smpte convention, matching what streamers ship today. rules & restrictions - renders only. subtitle selection is kit surface, and . selecting a track without this plugin loaded changes state correctly and paints nothing. see subtitles & text tracks. - ass/ssa is not this plugin's job. /nomercy-video-player/plugins-adapters/octopus renders those. the two coexist safely: they react to different signals, native cue events here and the selection event there, and each tears its own rendering down for formats it does not own. - colors resolve through a canvas-normalised hex conversion, with an alpha byte folded in from , and . so any css color string works in , not only hex literals. how to extend it there's no subclass hook, the plugin is a leaf consumer of and . a genuinely different rendering strategy canvas-based, webgl, a different cue-collision algorithm is a new plugin against the same two signals rather than a subclass of this one: don't register both and a custom renderer for the same format at once, both would paint the same cue stream independently and double up the dom. next steps - plugin: octopus ass/ssa subtitles: the renderer for the format this plugin intentionally leaves alone.

title: Plugin: Octopus (ASS/SSA Subtitles)
description: OctopusPlugin: libass-based ASS/SSA rendering via the NoMercy nomercy-subtitle-octopus fork, embedded-font support, and graceful degradation when the peer is absent.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player/src/plugins/octopus/index.ts / plugin: octopus ass/ssa subtitles vtt subtitles render out of the box through /nomercy-video-player/plugins-adapters/subtitle-overlay. ass/ssa the format anime releases and many other fansubs ship, carrying fonts, positioning, and karaoke effects vtt can't express needs an actual libass renderer. id is that renderer, a bridge over , the nomercy fork of libass-wasm with auth pre-fetch, cross-origin worker support, and canvas geometry fixes built in. options | option | type | default | purpose | |---|---|---|---| | | | bundled url | modern webassembly worker script. | | | | — | fallback for browsers without webassembly. optional, the modern path alone is fine for current browsers. | | | | — | font used when a subtitle requests one not in the resolved font set. | | | | | plugin-level static font urls, in addition to whatever the playlist item's own field resolves. | | | | — | renderer target fps. | | | | | rendering strategy passed straight to the underlying renderer. | | | | — | lazy-load subtitle file chunks, useful for very large ass files. | | | | — | internal scaler ratio. | | | | | frames the renderer pre-computes ahead of . higher smooths heavy ass effects at the cost of memory. | | | | — | toggle debug logging in the upstream worker. | activation flow the plugin listens to the player's event, when a track is selected, it resolves the url from the player's subtitle track list and checks the extension. non-ass/ssa urls tear the renderer down native or handle those instead, so and coexist safely, whichever format is actually selected drives the correct one. for an ass file that isn't part of the playlist item's array at all, call the plugin's own directly: font resolution fonts come from the item's typed field: either a manifest url, or a list of direct font file urls. see /nomercy-video-player/reference/types. both kinds can be present. the plugin fetches whichever is there and resolves each through the player's pipeline, so and auth apply. the plugin-level static option is always merged alongside what the item resolves. it is not a fallback for items with none. so a font family every track needs, a house fallback glyph set for instance, belongs there rather than on every item. rules & restrictions - is a regular dependency of . it ships with the package, and is not an optional peer to install separately. - all network i/o for the subtitle body and font binaries goes through the kit's auth-aware . the libass worker receives pre-fetched content as blob urls or inline strings, and never performs authenticated xhr of its own. - if the dynamic import of the renderer fails, the plugin degrades quietly. it logs one warning, and every later or call becomes a no-op rather than throwing. - blob urls for font binaries are tracked and revoked when the renderer tears down, on item change, track change or plugin dispose. nothing to clean up by hand. how to extend it the renderer instance itself is exposed for advanced consumers that need to reach into libass directly, the plugin retains lifecycle ownership either way: next steps - plugin: subtitle overlay: the vtt-rendering counterpart this plugin coexists with.
